# ===========================================================================
# THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE TAG SET -- TWO TIERS, AND THE DIFFERENCE
# BETWEEN THEM IS A HARD API LIMIT, NOT AN EDITORIAL CHOICE.
# ===========================================================================
#
# TIER 1 -- [TOPICS]. GitHub repo topics. Capped at TWENTY by the server; the
#   API rejects the 21st. Nothing written here changes that. These are the
#   structured, browsable tags: each becomes a crawlable github.com/topics/<t>
#   page, which is the highest-value discovery surface a repo has.
#
# TIER 2 -- [SIGNATURE]. The README signature block. NO LIMIT. Visible markdown
#   text is what survives GitHub's sanitizer intact, which makes it the true
#   descendant of the old forum signature. Everything true belongs here.
#
# THE RULE THAT GOVERNS BOTH TIERS: every tag must name something GENUINELY
# PRESENT IN THIS TREE. A tag is a claim about the repository, and a claim
# nobody checked is exactly the kind of decoration this project refuses
# everywhere else. The count beside each tag below is the number of tracked
# files containing that term, measured with:
#
#   git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -lIi "<tag>" | wc -l
#
# Re-measure rather than trusting these numbers; if a tag's evidence has gone
# to zero, the honest move is to DELETE THE TAG, not to keep advertising it.
